questions.question: If x - y = 4 and xy = 3, then what is the value of x³ - y³?
questions.solution:
Given:

x - y = 4 

xy = 3

Concept used:

x³ - y³ = (x - y) (x² + xy + y²)

(x - y)² = x² - 2xy + y²

Calculation:

x - y = 4

⇒ x² - 2xy + y² = 16

⇒ x2 + xy + y2 = 16 + (3 × 3)

⇒ x2 + xy + y2 = 25

⇒ (x - y) (x2 + xy + y2) = 25 × 4

⇒ (x - y) (x2 + xy + y2) = 100

⇒ x³ - y³ = 100

**∴ The value of x3 - y3 is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**⇒ If, x - y = k, then x³ - y³ = k³ + 3k × xy.

**∴ x³ - y³ = (4)³ + 3 × 4 × 3 = 64 + 36 = 100.**

questions.question: The ratio of the volume of first and second cylinder is 32 ∶ 9 and the ratio of their heights is 8 ∶ 9. If the area of the base of the second cylinder is 616 cm², then what will be the radius of the first cylinder?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Volumes** (V₁/V₂) = (r₁/r₂)² × (h₁/h₂)

32/9 = (r₁/r₂)² × (8/9) ⇒ (r₁/r₂)² = 4 ⇒ r₁/r₂ = 2/1

**Base Area** of second cylinder = 616 cm² ⇒ πr₂² = 616 ⇒ r₂ = 14 cm

**Radius** of first cylinder (r₁) = 2 × r₂ = 2 × 14 = 28 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 28 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of **Volumes** = 32 : 9, Ratio of **Heights** = 8 : 9, **Base Area** of 2ⁿd cylinder = 616 cm².

**Formula Used:** Volume of **Cylinder** = Base Area × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/acd11ded285ffb9d0a1886a97b13357940389a3d8856036753a3263898651acd.png] 

⇒ V₁ / V₂ = (Area₁ × h₁) / (Area₂ × h₂)

⇒ 32 / 9 = (Area₁ / 616) × (8 / 9)

⇒ 32 / 8 = Area₁ / 616

⇒ Area₁ = 4 × 616 = 2464 cm²

⇒ π × r₁² = 2464

⇒ 22/7 × r₁² = 2464

⇒ r₁² = (2464 × 7) / 22 = 112 × 7 = 784

⇒ r₁ = √784 = 28 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 28 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cylinder

The volume (V) is calculated as the product of the base area and the height: V = πr²h.

Surface Area of a Cylinder

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh and Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(r + h).

Radius and Area Relation

If the base area is A, then the radius r = √(A/π). For A = 616 cm², r = 14 cm.</p

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill an empty tank in 30 minutes and 40 minutes, respectively. Both pipes are opened for x minutes and then B is closed and A continues to fill. If the tank was completely filled in a total time of 22(1)/(2) minutes, then what is the value of 'x'?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = **LCM**(30, 40) = 120 units.

Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 4 units/min and **Pipe B** = 3 units/min.

Pipe A works for the entire 22.5 minutes: 4 × 22.5 = 90 units.

Remaining work done by Pipe B in **x** minutes: 120 − 90 = 30 units.

Value of **x** = 30 ÷ 3 = 10 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time of Pipe A = 30 min, Filling time of Pipe B = 40 min, Total time taken = 22.5 min.

**Formula Used:** Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Total capacity of the tank = **LCM** of 30 and 40 = 120 units.

⇒ Total time the tank was filling = 22 1/2 min = 22.5 min.

⇒ Since **Pipe A** was open the entire time, work done by A = 4 × 22.5 = 90 units.

⇒ Remaining work must be completed by **Pipe B** during its **x** minutes of operation.

⇒ Work done by Pipe B = Total work − Work by Pipe A = 120 − 90 = 30 units.

⇒ x = Work by B ÷ Efficiency of B = 30 ÷ 3 = 10 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Pipe Efficiency

When multiple pipes are open, their individual efficiencies are added to find the net filling rate: Net E = E₁ + E₂ + ... + Eₙ.

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes perform **positive work** (filling), while outlet pipes or leaks perform **negative work** (emptying) on the tank.

Time and Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task: Efficiency ∝ 1 / Time.</p

questions.question: A vegetable seller has a faulty weight of 2 kg which is 100 g less than the actual weight. He sold 2 kg of potatoes to a customer using the same faulty weight for Rs. 44. The cost price of potatoes to the seller was Rs. 18 per kg. How much profit did he earn on selling the potatoes?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **actual weight** delivered: 2 kg − 100 g = **1.9 kg**.

Calculate total **Cost Price (CP)** for the actual weight: 1.9 kg × Rs. 18/kg = **Rs. 34.2**.

Given **Selling Price (SP)** for the transaction = **Rs. 44**.

**Profit** = SP − CP = 44 − 34.2 = **Rs. 9.8**.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 9.8.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Faulty weight = 2 kg (100 g less), **CP** = Rs. 18/kg, **Total SP** = Rs. 44.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Total CP = Actual Weight × Rate per kg.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72544b8800525d6e1e513c841026b6af5b5a2cd32ea60c7e04cfb31e80488013.png] 

⇒ **Actual Weight** used by seller = 2000 g − 100 g = **1900 g** or **1.9 kg**.

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** of 1.9 kg = 1.9 × 18 = **Rs. 34.2**.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** of the quantity = **Rs. 44**.

⇒ **Profit** = 44 − 34.2 = **Rs. 9.8**.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 9.8.**

**__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer uses **faulty weights**, the profit is calculated on the **actual weight** delivered to the customer, as that represents the seller's true investment.

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit % = (Total Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100. In this case, Profit % = (9.8 ÷ 34.2) × 100 ≈ 28.65%.</p

questions.question: Ramesh’s salary is 20 percent more than Raman’s salary. If Ramesh saves Rs. 33750 which is 75 percent of his salary, then what is Raman’s salary?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Ramesh's Salary** = Savings × (100 / Savings%) = 33750 × (100 / 75) = 45000.

Ratio of **Ramesh : Raman** = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.

Since 6 units = 45000, then 1 unit = 7500.

**Raman's Salary** = 5 units = 5 × 7500 = 37500.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 37500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Ramesh's savings** = Rs. 33750, **Savings percentage** = 75%, **Salary comparison** = Ramesh is 20% more than Raman.

**Formula:** Income = Savings ÷ Savings%; Raman Salary = Ramesh Salary ÷ 1.20

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de152202477a35ebbe667d70a66e10edb43161d57ee491a297e43c9336cb5a79.png] 

⇒ Let **Ramesh's salary** be SR and **Raman's salary** be SM.

⇒ 75% of SR = 33750

⇒ (75 / 100) × SR = 33750

⇒ SR = (33750 × 100) ÷ 75 = 45000

⇒ SR = 120% of SM (Since Ramesh is 20% more than Raman)

⇒ 45000 = 1.20 × SM

⇒ SM = 45000 ÷ 1.20

⇒ SM = 450000 ÷ 12 = 37500

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 37500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase

If A is x% more than B, then A = B × (1 + x/100). To find B from A, use B = A ÷ (1 + x/100).

Income and Savings Relationship

Income = Expenditure + Savings. If savings are given as a percentage of income, then Income = Savings ÷ (Savings percentage / 100).

Fractional Conversions

Common percentages in fractions: 75% = 3/4, 20% = 1/5, 120% = 6/5. Using fractions often simplifies multi-step calculations.</p

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 140. If their LCM is 240 and HCF is 20, then find the smaller number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the numbers be 20x and 20y (where x and y are co-prime).

Sum: 20(x + y) = 140 ⇒ x + y = 7

LCM: 20xy = 240 ⇒ xy = 12

Numbers with sum 7 and product 12 are 3 and 4.

Smaller number = 20 × 3 = 60.

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of numbers (A + B) = 140, **LCM** = 240, **HCF** = 20.

**Formula Used:** Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf8f24327b08bcbb35949d6829efa949eb5d71926fe27677fe88607a22054c5d.png] 

⇒ A × B = 20 × 240 = 4800

⇒ We know (A − B)² = (A + B)² − 4AB

⇒ (A − B)² = (140)² − 4(4800)

⇒ (A − B)² = 19600 − 19200 = 400

⇒ A − B = √400 = 20

⇒ Adding (A + B = 140) and (A − B = 20): 2A = 160 ⇒ A = 80

⇒ Subtracting: 2B = 120 ⇒ B = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Property

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is always equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

Co-prime Relationship

If HCF of two numbers is h, then the numbers can be represented as hx and hy, where x and y are co-prime (HCF of x and y is 1).

LCM of Fractions

LCM of fractions = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (HCF of denominators).</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought an oven for ₹25,000 and sold it for ₹29,500. He spent ₹1,500 as overheads. What is his loss or gain percentage (rounded off to the nearest integer)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Cost Price (CP)** = 25,000 + 1,500 (Overheads) = ₹26,500.

**Selling Price (SP)** = ₹29,500.

Total **Profit** = 29,500 − 26,500 = ₹3,000.

**Profit %** = (3,000 ÷ 26,500) × 100 ≈ 11.32%.

Rounding to the nearest integer, we get **11%**.

**∴ The correct answer is Gain by 11%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Purchase Price = ₹25,000

Overhead Expenses = ₹1,500

Selling Price (SP) = ₹29,500

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97714c7b82c4586c8ab1b58d7cb2d3a956a8f920c0085ef5b2ecce915e24f869.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Total CP = Buying Price + Overhead Expenses

Gain % = [(SP − Total CP) ÷ Total CP] × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP = 25,000 + 1,500 = ₹26,500

⇒ Profit = SP − Total CP = 29,500 − 26,500 = ₹3,000

⇒ Profit % = (3,000 ÷ 26,500) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (300 ÷ 26.5) = 11.3207...

⇒ Rounding to the nearest integer = 11%

**∴ The correct answer is Gain by 11%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Cost Price

When a person buys an item and spends extra money on transportation, repairs, or labor, these **overheads** are added to the initial purchase price to find the effective cost price.

Gain and Loss Condition

If **SP > CP**, it is a **Gain**. If **CP > SP**, it is a **Loss**. Gain/Loss % is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**.

Rounding Off Rule

If the decimal part is 0.5 or more, round up to the next integer. If it is less than 0.5, the integer remains the same (e.g., 11.32 becomes 11).

questions.question: If three numbers are in the ratio 5 : 6 : 8 and the sum of their squares is 1250, then the product of those numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of numbers = **5 : 6 : 8**

Sum of squares of ratio parts = 5² + 6² + 8² = 25 + 36 + 64 = **125**

Common factor **x²** = Total Sum of Squares ÷ Ratio Sum = 1250 ÷ 125 = 10 ⇒ **x = √10**

Product = (5 × 6 × 8) × x³ = 240 × (√10)³ = 240 × 10√10 = **2400√10**

**∴ The correct answer is 2400√10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio = **5 : 6 : 8**, Sum of squares = **1250**

**Formula:** Let numbers be **ax, bx, cx**; then (ax)² + (bx)² + (cx)² = S

⇒ Let the numbers be **5x, 6x, and 8x**.

⇒ (5x)² + (6x)² + (8x)² = 1250

⇒ 25x² + 36x² + 64x² = 1250

⇒ 125x² = 1250

⇒ x² = 10

⇒ x = **√10**

⇒ Product = 5x × 6x × 8x = 240x³

⇒ Product = 240 × (√10)³ = 240 × 10√10 = **2400√10**

**∴ The correct answer is 2400√10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion Basics

When terms are in ratio a:b:c, they can be represented as ax, bx, and cx where x is a **common constant**.

Compound Ratio

The product of multiple ratios a:b and c:d is given by the **compound ratio** (ac):(bd).

Square Root Property

For any positive number n, (√n)³ = n√n. This is essential for **volumetric or product calculations** involving square roots.</p

questions.question: There is 20% iron in 1 Kg. mixture of sand and iron. How much sand must be added to the mixture to make the iron content 10%?
questions.solution:
**__Calculation:__**

In 1 kg mixture of sand and iron, there is 20% iron

⇒ In 1000g mixture, there is 200g iron.

Let, x gram of sand be added.

⇒ Ratio of iron = (200)/(1000+x) = (10)/(100) (given)

⇒ (200)/(1000+x) = (1)/(10)

⇒ 2000 = 1000 + x

⇒ x = 1000g = 1 kg

**∴ 1 kg sand must be added to the mixture to make the iron content 10%.**

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AD is the angle bisector of angle A. If AB = 8.4 cm and AC = 5.6 cm and DC = 2.8 cm, then the length of side BC will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of the sides **AB** : **AC** = 8.4 : 5.6 = 3 : 2.

By the **Angle Bisector Theorem**, the ratio of the segments **BD** : **DC** must also be 3 : 2.

Given **DC** = 2.8 cm, which represents 2 units, thus 1 unit = 1.4 cm.

The total length of side **BC** is (3 + 2) = 5 units.

Length of **BC** = 5 × 1.4 = 7 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In triangle **ABC**, **AD** is the **angle bisector** of angle **A**.

**AB** = 8.4 cm, **AC** = 5.6 cm, **DC** = 2.8 cm.

**Formula Used:**

**Internal Angle Bisector Theorem:** The internal bisector of an angle of a triangle divides the opposite side into segments that are proportional to the adjacent sides. ⇒ **AB** / **AC** = **BD** / **DC**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bb53d86d85eac74465ec9d2e058b4af53ed2cd68b0c89c899dde28f4253ef8fb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **AB** / **AC** = **BD** / **DC**

⇒ 8.4 / 5.6 = **BD** / 2.8

⇒ (84 / 56) = **BD** / 2.8

⇒ 1.5 = **BD** / 2.8

⇒ **BD** = 1.5 × 2.8

⇒ **BD** = 4.2 cm

Now, side **BC** = **BD** + **DC**

⇒ **BC** = 4.2 + 2.8

⇒ **BC** = 7 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 7 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Internal Angle Bisector Theorem

In any triangle, the angle bisector divides the opposite side into two segments whose lengths have the same ratio as the other two sides of the triangle.

Length of the Angle Bisector

The length of the internal bisector **AD** can be calculated using the formula: **AD**² = (**AB** × **AC**) − (**BD** × **DC**).

External Angle Bisector Theorem

If the external bisector of angle **A** intersects the extended side **BC** at **E**, then **AB** / **AC** = **BE** / **CE**.</p

questions.question: The base of a right prism is a triangle with sides 21 cm, 72 cm and 75 cm. Its height is 14 cm. The lateral surface area (in cm²) and the volume (in cm³) are, respectively:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the base triangle: Sides 21, 72, 75 are in ratio 7 : 24 : 25, which is a **Pythagorean Triplet**.

**Lateral Surface Area (LSA)** = Perimeter × Height = (21 + 72 + 75) × 14 = 168 × 14 = 2352 cm².

**Volume** = Base Area × Height = (1/2 × 21 × 72) × 14 = 756 × 14 = 10584 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 2352 cm² and 10584 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sides of the triangular base: **a = 21 cm**, **b = 72 cm**, **c = 75 cm**.

Height of the prism: **h = 14 cm**.

Check if the base is a right-angled triangle:

⇒ 21² + 72² = 441 + 5184 = 5625

⇒ 75² = 5625

⇒ Since 21² + 72² = 75², the base is a **right-angled triangle**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d8b3bc16a69db8ffd1c6226a023b494884547309aa392cdc063f8a22bf6de14c.png] 

**1. Calculation for Lateral Surface Area (LSA):**

⇒ Perimeter of base = a + b + c

⇒ Perimeter = 21 + 72 + 75 = 168 cm

⇒ LSA = Perimeter × height

⇒ LSA = 168 × 14

⇒ LSA = 2352 cm²

**2. Calculation for Volume:**

⇒ Area of base = (1/2) × base × perpendicular height

⇒ Area of base = (1/2) × 21 × 72 = 21 × 36

⇒ Area of base = 756 cm²

⇒ Volume = Area of base × height of prism

⇒ Volume = 756 × 14

⇒ Volume = 10584 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 2352 cm² and 10584 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Right Prism Formulas

Lateral Surface Area = Perimeter of base × Height. Total Surface Area = LSA + 2 × Base Area. Volume = Base Area × Height.

Pythagorean Triplets

A set of three integers (a, b, c) such that a² + b² = c². Common scaled triplets include (7, 24, 25), (3, 4, 5), and (5, 12, 13).

Area of Scalene Triangle

If the base is not right-angled, use Heron's formula: Area = √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)), where s = (a+b+c)/2.</p

questions.question: A boat can travel 104 km downstream in 8 hours. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/h, then find in what time will it be able to cover 13 km upstream?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Downstream speed = 104 ÷ 8 = 13 km/h.

Upstream speed = Downstream speed − (2 × Speed of stream)

Upstream speed = 13 − (2 × 2) = 9 km/h.

Time for 13 km upstream = 13 ÷ 9 = 1 4/9 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 4/9 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Downstream distance = 104 km

Downstream time = 8 hours

Speed of stream (v) = 2 km/h

Upstream distance = 13 km

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Downstream speed (D) = u + v

Upstream speed (U) = u − v

Where u = speed of boat in still water and v = speed of stream.

 
• 
 

 Downstream: 104 km / 8 hrs = 13 km/h
 
• 
 

 Upstream: Distance = 13 km
 Result: Time = 13 ÷ 9 = 1 4/9 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream speed (D) = 104 ÷ 8 = 13 km/h

⇒ u + v = 13

⇒ u + 2 = 13

⇒ u = 13 − 2 = 11 km/h

⇒ Upstream speed (U) = u − v = 11 − 2 = 9 km/h

⇒ Time taken = Distance ÷ Upstream speed

⇒ Time taken = 13 ÷ 9 = 1 4/9 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 1 4/9 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speed

Downstream speed (D) = Speed of boat in still water (u) + Speed of stream (v). Upstream speed (U) = u − v.

Speed of Boat in Still Water

The speed of the boat in still water can be calculated as u = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of the Stream

The speed of the current or stream can be calculated as v = (D − U) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: In ΔXYZ, P and Q are the points on sides XY and XZ respectively. PQ is parallel to YZ and PQ ∶ YZ = 3 ∶ 8. If XY = 88 cm, then what is the length of XP?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **PQ || YZ**, by the **Basic Proportionality Theorem**, ΔXPQ is similar to ΔXYZ.

The ratio of corresponding sides is equal: XP / XY = PQ / YZ

XP / XY = 3 / 8

Given XY = 88 cm (which corresponds to 8 units).

8 units = 88 cm ⇒ 1 unit = 11 cm.

XP = 3 units = 3 × 11 = 33 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 33 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In ΔXYZ, PQ || YZ, XY = 88 cm, and PQ ÷ YZ = 3 ÷ 8.

**Formula Used:**

In two similar triangles, the ratio of corresponding sides is constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2a68d5e22b051d319180f61e07520ec70a163b67a8fc4bfd0fec2e97923ca2e.png] 

**Calculations:**

Since PQ || YZ, corresponding angles are equal:

∠XPQ = ∠XYZ and ∠XQP = ∠XZY

∴ ΔXPQ ∼ ΔXYZ (By AA similarity criterion)

⇒ XP / XY = PQ / YZ

⇒ XP / 88 = 3 / 8

⇒ XP = 88 × (3 / 8)

⇒ XP = 11 × 3

⇒ XP = 33 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 33 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales's Theorem)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio: XP/PY = XQ/QZ.

Area Ratio of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(ΔXPQ)/Area(ΔXYZ) = (PQ/YZ)².

AA Similarity Criterion

If two angles of one triangle are respectively equal to two angles of another triangle, then the two triangles are similar.</p

questions.question: If 46.3506 = 4A + (6)/(B) + 3C + (5)/(D) + 6E, then find the value of (A + B + C + D + E).

The distance between station A and station B is 610 km. Train P starts from station A at 08:00 A.M with a speed of 70 kmph towards station B. At 09:00 A.M Train Q starts from the station B with speed of 20 kmph. Find the time at which they meet.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Distance** at 09:00 A.M. = 610 − (70 × 1) = 540 km.

**Relative Speed** (opposite direction) = 70 + 20 = 90 kmph.

**Time to meet** = 540 ÷ 90 = 6 hours after 09:00 A.M.

**Meeting Time** = 09:00 A.M. + 6 hours = 03:00 P.M.

**∴ The correct answer is 03:00 P.M.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3098319a07db2a3553a75b388103582437a97c7c5f991ba33c8b43a261268af.png] 

**Given:** Total Distance = 610 km, Speed P = 70 kmph, Speed Q = 20 kmph.

**Formula:** Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Distance covered by **Train P** from 08:00 A.M. to 09:00 A.M. = 70 × 1 = 70 km.

⇒ Remaining distance at 09:00 A.M. = 610 − 70 = 540 km.

⇒ Since trains move in **opposite directions**, Relative Speed = 70 + 20 = 90 kmph.

⇒ Time taken to meet = 540 ÷ 90 = 6 hours.

⇒ Meeting time = 09:00 A.M. + 6 hours = 15:00 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 03:00 P.M.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). If moving in the **same direction**, it is the **difference** (S₁ − S₂).

Meeting Point Formula

Meeting time = (Initial distance between them at the **same starting time**) ÷ (Relative Speed).

Average Speed

For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y). For unequal distances, it is Total Distance ÷ Total Time.</p

questions.question: sqrt2 - sqrt3 is :
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The difference between two **distinct irrational numbers** (√2 and √3) where neither is a multiple of the other by a rational factor always results in an **irrational number**.

√2 ≈ 1.4142... and √3 ≈ 1.7320...

√2 − √3 ≈ −0.3178... which is **non-terminating** and **non-repeating**.

Such decimals represent **irrational numbers**.

**∴ The correct answer is an irrational number.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a66fef762b3a499b37e614dd1f5485f2dbf4ae6963c6d7808ebf924a22ec4b1a.png] 

**Given:** The expression is √2 − √3.

**Method:** Proof by **Contradiction**.

⇒ Let us assume that √2 − √3 = r, where r is a **rational number**.

⇒ Squaring both sides: (√2 − √3)² = r²

⇒ (√2)² + (√3)² − 2(√2 × √3) = r²

⇒ 2 + 3 − 2√6 = r²

⇒ 5 − 2√6 = r²

⇒ 5 − r² = 2√6

⇒ √6 = (5 − r²) / 2

⇒ Since r is rational, r² is rational, and (5 − r²) / 2 is also **rational**.

⇒ However, √6 is an **irrational number** (as 6 is not a perfect square).

⇒ An irrational number cannot be equal to a rational number.

⇒ This is a **contradiction**, so our assumption was wrong.

**∴ The correct answer is an irrational number.**

**__Additional Information__**

Irrational Numbers

These are numbers that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers (p/q). Their decimal expansion is **non-terminating** and **non-repeating**.

Properties of Irrationals

The sum or difference of a rational and an irrational number is always **irrational**. The sum or difference of two irrationals may be rational or irrational.

Square Roots of Primes

The **square root** of any **prime number** (like 2, 3, 5, 7, etc.) is always an irrational number.

Real Numbers

Real numbers are the union of **rational numbers** and **irrational numbers**. Every point on the number line represents a unique real number.</p

questions.question: The inner and outer radii of a hemispherical wooden bowl are 6 cm and 8 cm, respectively. Its entire surface has to be polished and the cost of polishing π cm² is Rs. 50. How much will it cost to polish the bowl?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a **hollow hemispherical bowl** = 3πR² + πr²

Given: **Outer radius (R)** = 8 cm and **Inner radius (r)** = 6 cm.

TSA = π(3 × 8² + 6²) = π(192 + 36) = 228π cm².

Cost of polishing π cm² = Rs. 50 ⇒ Total Cost = 228 × 50 = Rs. 11,400.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 11,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Inner radius (r) = 6 cm

Outer radius (R) = 8 cm

Polishing rate = Rs. 50 per π cm²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d2c3a9cf84f6e92bf787a35aac322ab838093c7448d0a6b1b73e8d95de841cff.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area = **Outer CSA** + **Inner CSA** + **Area of the Ring**

TSA = 2πR² + 2πr² + π(R² − r²)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Outer CSA = 2 × π × 8² = 128π cm²

⇒ Inner CSA = 2 × π × 6² = 72π cm²

⇒ Area of Top Ring = π(8² − 6²) = π(64 − 36) = 28π cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area = 128π + 72π + 28π = 228π cm²

⇒ Cost of polishing π cm² = Rs. 50

⇒ Total Polishing Cost = (228π / π) × 50

⇒ Total Polishing Cost = 228 × 50 = Rs. 11,400

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 11,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Hollow Hemisphere

The volume of the material of a hollow hemispherical bowl is given by V = (2/3)π(R³ − r³), where R is the outer radius and r is the inner radius.

Surface Area of a Solid Hemisphere

For a solid hemisphere of radius R, the total surface area is TSA = 3πR², which includes the curved surface (2πR²) and the flat circular base (πR²).

Surface Area of a Sphere

The total surface area of a complete sphere is 4πR², and its volume is (4/3)πR³.</p
